note: Adapted from the original description of Termes Buchholzi by Sjöstedt (1900), which combines a Latin diagnosis with a German description; only the alate is described, soldiers and workers being unrecorded; observations on swarming and on specimens taken at sea are not translated; numerical data such as head length and pronotal length are omitted because of damaged OCR, and specimen records are not translated.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body above reddish brown to yellowish red, abdomen paler; mouthparts, antennae, maxillary palps and the whole ventral surface together with the legs white, in dry specimens with varying degrees of yellow; head slightly flattened, with a small median protuberance that is sometimes rather indistinct; a fairly distinct ridge between the ocelli, the frons in front of the ridge slightly obliquely flattened; clypeus slightly paler than the frons, slightly raised, posterior margin weakly curved, anteriorly almost straight, with a dark median line, anterior half white, thin and flat, rounded in front; labrum ligulate, slightly longer than wide, thinning anteriorly, white, rounded, thickened within the apex; compound eyes rather large, round; ocelli broadly oval, separated from the compound eye by at most the length of their long diameter, usually closer, with a small pit obliquely mesad of them; antennae 19-segmented, the basal segment about as long as the following three segments together, the second segment longer than the third, the remaining segments subglobose, slightly shorter ventrally, slightly longer laterally; pronotum pilose, semicircular, anteriorly slightly curved, anterior margin slightly uprolled, middle almost imperceptibly notched; posterior margin flat and slightly concave; anterior angles concave; pronotum twice as wide as long, narrower than the head width between the compound eyes; posterior margins of meso- and metanotum broad, very distinctly rounded-concave, angles rounded; wings in alcohol semitransparent, milky glassy white with a yellowish red tinge, opaque when dry, with varying degrees of greyish brown; media and submedia of the fore wing fused near the wing base, but the point of fusion rather far out, so that 5–6 branches run to the posterior margin between the fusion point and the wing base; costa and subcosta pale yellow to brown, ending slightly before the apex; precostal area veinless; an orange-yellow stripe in the distal half beneath the subcosta, with many short downward branches; legs densely pilose, slightly surpassing the abdomen; hind tibia longer than the femur; apical tarsal segment slightly longer than the remaining segments together; abdominal appendages very small, wart-like. Wing span 50–55 mm, body length with wings 27–30 mm, wing length 22.3–25 mm, wing width 6.8–7.3 mm, body length with head 13–14 mm.
